You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "content": "# Continual ARC task-e6a91d46 — unsuccessful instance; evidence, not solved rule

Task ended at 8 incorrect submissions, 3 demo requests. Do not treat any attempted output as correct. Preserve this as cautionary task-family evidence.

## Grid setup
Each input has six separated hollow rectangular frames in various colors. Some frames contain an irregular internal pattern in the frame's own color; other frames are empty. The demos show a transformation applied to the interior cells of certain patterned frames, while some patterned frames and some empty frames are left untouched. Therefore do not indiscriminately copy one pattern to every empty frame, repaint all rectangles, or assume frame interiors are sources/targets solely based on similar dimensions.

## Demo 1 observations (19x19)
- Frame color 8 at rows 1–8, cols 1–8 contains irregular 7x7 interior pattern, and remains unchanged in output.
- Frame color 6 at rows 2–8, cols 11–18 starts blank; output interior changes to a sparse pattern of 6s.
- Frame color 4 at rows 11–17, cols 3–10 starts blank; output interior gets another pattern of 4s.
- Frame color 5 at rows 11–15, cols 13–17 is a partial/short empty frame and disappears completely in output (all its 5s erased).
This suggests a rule selectively operates on frames based on a relation between other pattern(s), dimensions, or structural criterion; specifics unresolved.

## Demo 2 observations (21x21)
- Color-3 frame rows 1–6, cols 7–11 starts empty and receives a 3-pattern in its 4x3 interior.
- Color-2 frame rows 2–7, cols 16–20 starts empty and receives a 2-pattern in its 4x3 interior.
- Color-4 frame rows 7–12, cols 1–5 starts empty and receives a 4-pattern in its 4x3 interior.
- Color-7 frame rows 16–19, cols 3–7 is empty and disappears.
- Color-5 frame rows 11–16, cols 11–15 has irregular pattern, remains unchanged.
The three recipients share equal interior dimensions (4x3); source/frame 5 pattern has 4x3 interior and appears a plausible donor. The exact copying/rotation/index rule was not correctly inferred in this run.

## Demo 3 observations (22x22)
- Color-2 frame rows 1–6, cols 5–11 starts empty and fills with an irregular 2 pattern (interior 4x5).
- Color-3 frame rows 3–6, cols 16–19 is empty and disappears.
- Color-8 shape rows 8–13, cols 0–6 has internal pattern and remains unchanged.
- Color-1 frame rows 12–17, cols 11–17 starts empty and fills with irregular 1 pattern (interior 4x5).
- Color-7 frame rows 15–21, cols 2–7 is empty and disappears.
Here two recipients have same 4x5 interior dimensions; patterned 8-frame interior is 4x5, again suggesting matching-dimension pattern donor. But recipient pattern seems not a straightforward simple copy as attempted guesses all failed. Need compare binary interior matrices carefully, including orientation/rotation/reflection and perhaps negative/inverted mask. Do not infer more from this unsolved evidence.

## Failed test attempts
Eight submissions all incorrect. They varied attempted fillings of initially empty frames and progressively guessed transfers from 7, 8, 5 or variations. No output correctness feedback beyond incorrect, so no individual guess may be marked as verified or as narrowing which frames/cells should change. In particular, do not reuse the produced guessed grids.

## Practical lesson
The useful cross-demo clue is that patterned donor panels appear to share exact interior dimensions with selected recipients (demo2: 4x3; demo3: 4x5). Some empty panels are erased, not filled, so there is a selector/structure rule beyond dimension compatibility. Future recurrence: first map each frame's interior binary matrix, dimensions, and position; identify exact selected source-to-target mapping and transformation (identity, rotations/reflections, complement, or another encoding) from demos; check which other frames disappear; build output changes only after this is established. Treat this note strictly as weak evidence from a failed instance.
"
}
